title: Org access compact view — quick actions & audit search notes
content:
Purpose
---
Working notes from the compact admin view workshop (goal: single-row, scannable org/team list that surfaces the most common quick actions for engineers/ops). This doc collects wireframe decisions, unanswered UX questions, and a prioritized backlog for the sprint.

High-level idea
---
Goal: reduce clicks for 80% of admin tasks. Provide an ops-first compact row for orgs and teams with: role badges, primary quick actions (create API key, create service account, view audit events), and a lightweight inline permission editor for rapid changes.

Key screens / components sketched
---
1) Compact org/team row (wireframe notes)
   - Left: org/team name, short description (optional).
   - Middle: role badges (owner, admin, billing, viewer). Click opens compact role modal.
   - Right cluster: quick actions — Create Key (primary CTA), New Service Account, Audit (opens audit timeline), More (dropdown: rename, delete, export config).
   - Visual affordances: subtle separator for teams under same org, small timestamp of last-change, and a tiny health indicator (green/yellow/red) driven by recent auth errors.

2) Inline permission editor (mini modal)
   - Opens from role badge. Shows current principals as tokens with ability to add (search) and remove.
   - Quick preview of effective permissions (simplified list: read/generate/billing/manage).
   - Save + audit-note field (free text) — required for org-level changes (configurable by policy).

3) API key quick flow
   - Click Create Key => 1-step modal: name, TTL (preset: 30d, 90d, custom), scopes (checkbox list simplified by common presets: full-api, generate-only, embeddings-only).
   - On create: show full secret once with emphasized copy instructions + download .json button. Show link to rotate/disable key from row.
   - UX constraint: for security, hide brute force of key list; show only metadata on list (last-used, created).

4) Service account flow
   - New Service Account button opens creation modal: name, attached roles (multi-select), key options (no key / one-time key / cert request).
   - Special case: option to create ephemeral key tied to workload identity (for private deployments).

5) Audit search panel (expanded view)
   - Quick filters row: actor, resource type (org/team/key/service-account), action type (create/update/delete, rotate, login), date range presets (last 24h, 7d, 30d), result size.
   - Timeline view: compact rows with color-coded severity (info/warning/error). Each row expand shows before/after JSON diff (collapsible).
   - Export button (CSV/JSON) + retention note (policy-linked).

Backlog / acceptance criteria (prioritized)
---
P0 (must-have for next ship)
 - Compact row with name, badges, and quick-actions implemented as accessible buttons.
 - Create Key modal + one-time secret reveal + download. Test: key appears in audit log as created event.
 - Audit quick-open from row and filter by that org/team pre-populated.

P1
 - Inline permission editor with add/remove principals + required audit-note for org-level changes.
 - Service account creation modal with key option.
 - Show last-used timestamp and health indicator on row.

P2
 - Advanced audit timeline with JSON diffs and export.
 - Ephemeral key generation for private deployments.
 - A/B test: compact row vs. full detail row for power users.

Open questions / risks
---
- RBAC model complexity: how to map existing granular permissions to simplified effective-perms shown in inline editor without misleading users? (Related: CONF-234)
- Do we require explicit audit note for every permission change? Ops likes it, UX team worries about friction for small changes. Consider policy toggle per org.
- API key TTL presets: legal/security team prefers shorter defaults for enterprise customers — need policy flow to override UI.
- Audit retention and export: large orgs will hit retention/size issues — need server-side pagination and async export.

Accessibility notes
---
- Compact row must be keyboard navigable; quick-actions should have clear aria-labels.
- Modals must trap focus and announce success states.

Implementation notes / engineering constraints
---
- Backend: need endpoints to create keys with TTL, generate one-time secret, and mark secret as viewed. Ensure creation event is atomic and logged.
- Audit: add lightweight (summary) and heavy (full diff) payloads to storage to support the timeline without expensive reads for list views.
- Permissions overlay: client should fetch role->capability mapping (cached) to render simplified effective-perms.
- Rate limits: creation of many keys/service accounts must be throttled - add debounce on UI to prevent spamming.

Design open items (for next sync)
---
- Microcopy for secret reveal modal (security-first language).
- Visual for health indicator: is error state an orange triangle or red dot? Suggest orange for warning, red for breach/severity.
- CTA placement: make Create Key the primary action for org rows but for teams where service accounts are primary, adjust ordering via feature flag.

Links / refs
---
- Confluence: Org Access Design (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira: PROD-4532 (compact access rows), PROD-4590 (keys backend work), SEC-918 (TTL policy)
